experiment: Run 27 — source-part registration under a straight-axis constraint
objective: Repair the previously rejected pen C result: straight exposed metal nib, source-like nib/body proportions and stepped connector, while retaining the existing body and composition.

arms.baseline: One ordinary built-in image edit with identical target and three references, explicit straightness/proportion/connector and preservation requirements; no retries.
arms.candidate: Register the actual reference front assembly (nib + stepped connector) once; map it rigidly to the existing body axis and diameter. Replace only the old front assembly, restore its plain background locally. No generated replacement part.

changed: Part pixels and geometry are determined from the reference instead of resynthesized by a generative model.
fixed: Target image, reference images, desired part geometry, body anchor, scene, crop and success criteria. No best-of selection.
manual_setup: Source front ROI and target old-front repair area/body attachment selected once by assistant. This is an assisted feasibility experiment, not automatic registration. Count registration edits, and record code execution separately from setup.

gates.straightness: Centerline p95 deviation <=1px at 1672px evaluation width; inspect silhouettes too because a line score alone is insufficient.
gates.proportion: Visible metal length/body diameter within 10% of the provided side reference, only for this approximately side-on target; not physical millimeter metrology.
gates.structure: Short stepped connector, distinct felt nib, no invented clip near the tip, no gap at the body join.
gates.preservation: No changes outside the declared front repair region for the candidate; report corresponding ordinary-edit change. Metric alone does not imply better overall appearance.
gates.overall: Visible local improvement over input and baseline without a new seam/background/material defect; user acceptance remains unmeasured.

stop: Do not tune after seeing baseline output. If no meaningful improvement, run one different supported case from available customer records rather than merely replacing the webpage.
limits: One known development failure, not unseen validation
Same approximate side view; not arbitrary novel-view generation
Plain background makes removal easier; no occluded-hand/background reconstruction claim
Catalog comparison image is a provided product reference, not calibrated target-view ground truth
